examples.en: A gentle breeze blows in through the window.
The spring breeze lightly brushing past feels nice.
The puppy gave its tail a light wag.
I saw the curtain sway gently.
My hair fluttered lightly, so I brushed it back with my hand.

examples.ko: 저녁이 되자 선선한 바람이 살랑 불기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When evening came, a cool breeze began to blow gently.

explain: 센 바람이 아니라 부드러운 바람이나 가벼운 흔들림에 써요. 말할 때는 '살랑살랑'처럼 반복해서 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The leaves are swaying lightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살랑'을 반복한 모양으로, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The repeated form of '살랑', used more often in speech.

phrases.en: The puppy wagged its tail lightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 기분 좋게 꼬리를 가볍게 흔드는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an animal softly wagging its tail happily.

phrases.en: Her skirt hem flutters lightly in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가벼운 옷이 부드럽게 움직이는 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits light clothing moving softly in the breeze.

explain_en: A light single movement, as with wind or a tail. It is used for soft breezes or light swaying, not strong wind. In speech, people often repeat it as '살랑살랑'.

t90.ax: I saw the curtain sway gently.

en: to revive; to recover; to come back

examples.ko: 죽은 줄 알았던 화분이 비를 맞고 소생했어요.
examples.en: The pot plant I thought was dead revived in the rain.
When spring comes, all of nature comes back to life.

examples.ko: 쓰러졌던 환자가 응급 치료로 소생해서 의사들이 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: The patient who had collapsed was revived by emergency treatment, and the doctors were glad.

examples.ko: 다친 새가 소생하길 바라며 따뜻하게 해 줬어요.
examples.en: I kept the injured bird warm, hoping it would revive.

examples.ko: 도시 경제가 소생하는 데 몇 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took several years for the city's economy to revive.
New leaves came out on the tree that revived.

explain: 죽은 듯하던 사람, 식물, 자연이 다시 살아날 때 써요. 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. 아팠던 사람이 기운을 되찾는 정도라면 '회복하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: When it rained, the withered grass came back to life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 쉬워서 일상 대화에서 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but easier, and natural in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The doctor revived the person who had collapsed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 살아나게 만드는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of bringing something back to life.

phrases.example: 이 화분은 물을 주면 소생할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This plant can revive if you water it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 살아날 가능성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the possibility of coming back to life.

explain_en: Formal, written, plants or people recovering from near death. Use it when something that seemed dead, such as a person, a plant or nature, comes back to life. It appears more in writing and the news. If a sick person merely regains strength, 회복하다 sounds more natural.

dis.h: recover from near death; formal, written
gh: come back to life; everyday, native word
pull through; recover from a crisis

p.n: 살아나다 is the everyday way to say it; 소생하다 sounds literary.

t90.ax: New leaves came out on the tree that revived.

examples.en: When May came, the mountains filled with fresh green.
I walked along a forest path thick with fresh greenery.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤라 신록이 더 싱그러워요.
examples.en: It rained, so the fresh green looks even more vibrant.
Looking at the fresh green outside the window calms my mind.
I want to travel in the season of fresh green leaves.
In every park the fresh green shines dazzlingly.

explain: 봄이 끝나고 초여름으로 가며 새로 난 잎이 푸르게 올라온 모습을 말해요. 가을의 '단풍'과 짝처럼 계절 느낌을 줘서 글이나 인사말에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: May is the season of fresh green leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 초여름 무렵을 아름답게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lovely way to refer to early summer.

phrases.en: The fresh green gets deeper day by day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잎의 초록색이 점점 진해지는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the green of the leaves getting deeper.

phrases.en: I enjoyed the fresh greenery in the park on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산책이나 소풍에서 푸른 잎을 보며 즐길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when enjoying green leaves on a walk or picnic.

explain_en: It describes the fresh new leaves turning bright green as spring moves into early summer. It pairs in feeling with autumn's '단풍' and often appears in writing and seasonal greetings.

examples.ko: 산 정상에 넓은 억새밭이 펼쳐져 있어요.
examples.en: A wide field of silver grass stretches out at the mountain top.
Last weekend we took a family photo in the silver grass field.

examples.ko: 바람이 불자 억새밭이 은빛 물결처럼 일렁였어요.
examples.en: When the wind blew, the field rippled like silver waves.

examples.ko: 억새밭 사이로 좁은 길이 나 있어요.
examples.en: A narrow path runs through the silver grass field.
Every autumn, people flock to see the silver grass fields.
There is a small cafe near the silver grass field.

explain: 억새가 넓게 자란 곳을 말해요. 가을 나들이나 여행 이야기에서 '억새밭이 펼쳐지다', '억새밭을 걷다'처럼 자주 써요. 억새를 보러 가는 곳이 많아서 가을이면 안내문에도 나와요.

phrases.en: I walked through the silver grass field with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억새가 가득한 길을 산책할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking a walk through a field full of silver grass.
phrases.en_equiv: to walk through a silver grass field

phrases.en: I want to go to a silver grass field in autumn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소로 가는 계획을 말할 때 조사 '에'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the particle 에 to talk about plans to go there.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to a silver grass field

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the path through the silver grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억새밭 사이로 난 길을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a path running through the silver grass field.

explain_en: It refers to a place where silver grass grows over a wide area. In stories about autumn outings and trips, you often hear '억새밭이 펼쳐지다' and '억새밭을 걷다'. Many places are visited just to see silver grass, so the word often appears on notices in autumn.

examples.ko: 아침 해가 바다 위로 찬란히 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: The morning sun rose radiantly over the sea.
The stars shine brilliantly in the night sky.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 오래전에 찬란히 꽃핀 문화를 가졌어요.
examples.en: This city had a culture that bloomed magnificently long ago.
The chandelier sparkled brilliantly from the ceiling.
His name remained in history with glory.

examples.ko: 졸업하는 날 아침 해가 찬란히 빛났어요.
examples.en: On graduation day, the morning sun shone brilliantly.

explain: 눈부시게 빛나는 모습이나, 훌륭하고 화려한 역사·문화를 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서 가볍게 쓰기보다 글이나 감동적인 장면에서 많이 보여요. 형용사는 '찬란하다'예요.

phrases.en: The sunlight pours down brilliantly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '찬란히'와 뜻이 같고, 문장에서 동사 앞에 자연스럽게 이어져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 찬란히, flowing naturally before a verb.

phrases.en: We took photos under the dazzling sunshine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '찬란하다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: Korea has many splendid cultural heritage sites.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훌륭하고 화려한 역사나 문화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a magnificent history or culture.

explain_en: Magnificently radiant; literary, formal, sunrise or achievements. It describes something shining dazzlingly, or a splendid history or culture. It appears more in writing and moving scenes than in light everyday talk. The adjective form is '찬란하다'.

t90.ax: His name remained in history with glory.

examples.en: When the power went out, the room became pitch dark.

examples.ko: 칠흑 같은 밤길을 혼자 걸으니 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Walking alone on the pitch-dark night road was scary.

examples.ko: 할머니는 젊을 때 칠흑 같은 머리카락이 아름다웠대요.
examples.en: They say my grandmother's jet-black hair was beautiful when she was young.

examples.ko: 산속은 칠흑 같은 어둠에 싸여 있었어요.
examples.en: The mountains were wrapped in pitch-black darkness.
There was no moon, so the sky was jet-black.

examples.ko: 칠흑 속에서 작은 불빛이 하나 보였어요.
examples.en: A small light appeared in the pitch darkness.

explain: 거의 '칠흑 같은 어둠/밤', '칠흑같이 어둡다'처럼 굳은 짝으로 써요. 머리카락이나 눈동자가 아주 까만 것도 비유로 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '깜깜하다', '캄캄하다'가 더 가벼운 말이에요.

phrases.example: 칠흑 같은 어둠 속에서 길을 찾기 어려웠어요.
phrases.en: It was hard to find the way in the pitch-black darkness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 깊은 어둠을 말하는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for very deep darkness.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 칠흑 같은 머리카락이 예뻐요.
phrases.en: That actor's jet-black hair is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 새까만 머리카락을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for very black hair.

phrases.en: The room was dark, so I turned on the light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칠흑보다 가볍고 일상에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter, everyday word compared with 칠흑.

explain_en: It is mostly used in fixed pairings such as '칠흑 같은 어둠/밤' and '칠흑같이 어둡다'. It can also describe very black hair or eyes figuratively. In everyday talk, '깜깜하다' and '캄캄하다' are the lighter words.

examples.en: My ears were numb in the icy wind of the winter morning.
An icy wind is blowing, so I don't want to go out.
When I went out to the Han River, the wind was really biting.
I waited for the bus in the biting wind.

examples.ko: 오늘은 칼바람 때문에 체감온도가 더 낮아요.
examples.en: Today the felt temperature is lower because of the icy wind.

examples.ko: 이럴 땐 목도리로 칼바람을 막아야 해요.
examples.en: At times like this you have to block the icy wind with a scarf.

explain: '찬바람'보다 훨씬 날카롭게 살을 에는 듯한 겨울바람에 써요. 보통 '칼바람이 불다/몰아치다'라고 해요. 글에서는 '삭풍'이라는 말도 있지만 대화에서는 '칼바람'이 더 가까운 말이에요.

phrases.en: A bitter wind is blowing today, so it's freezing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '칼바람'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often paired with 칼바람.

phrases.en: An icy wind lashed the mountaintop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 세게 계속 불 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the wind blows strongly and continuously.

phrases.en: Cold wind is coming in through the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: '칼바람'보다 덜 날카로운, 일반적으로 차가운 바람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A milder, more general cold wind than 칼바람.

explain_en: It is used for a winter wind that feels sharper than a plain '찬바람' and cuts into the skin. You usually say '칼바람이 불다/몰아치다'. There is also the literary word '삭풍', but '칼바람' is closer to everyday speech.

examples.ko: 그 일을 가벼이 여기면 큰일 나요.
examples.en: If you take that matter lightly, you will be in big trouble.
Do not take what people say lightly.
The child greeted me with a light smile.

examples.ko: 약속을 가벼이 하는 사람은 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to trust someone who makes promises lightly.
A light breeze was blowing, and I felt good.

examples.ko: 작은 실수라고 가벼이 넘기지 말고 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: Do not brush it off as a small mistake. Be sure to check it.

explain: '가볍게'와 뜻은 비슷하지만 글이나 조금 점잖은 말에서 더 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '가볍게'를 훨씬 자연스럽게 말해요. '가벼이 여기다'는 어떤 일을 중요하게 보지 않는다는 뜻으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Don't take that matter lightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가벼이'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural in everyday conversation than 'gabyeoi'.

phrases.en: Don't treat even a small promise lightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 중요하게 보지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means not regarding something as important.

phrases.en: Don't take your friend's words lightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 말을 대수롭지 않게 듣는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means listening to someone's words as if they were not important.

explain_en: It is close to '가볍게' in meaning but suits writing or a slightly formal tone better. In everyday conversation '가볍게' sounds much more natural. '가벼이 여기다' often appears with the meaning of not treating something as important.

t90.ax: Do not take what people say lightly.

examples.ko: 제가 친구를 만났다고 남편이 강짜를 부려요.
examples.en: My husband throws a jealous fit because I met a friend.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 강짜가 심해서 연락이 조금만 늦어도 화를 내요.
examples.en: He is so jealous that he gets angry even if I'm a little late replying.

examples.ko: 괜한 강짜 부리지 말고 솔직하게 말해요.
examples.en: Don't throw a pointless jealous fit; just say it honestly.
Throwing a jealous fit like that is useless.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 아내가 강짜를 부리는 장면이 웃겼어요.
examples.en: The scene where the wife in the drama threw a jealous fit was funny.
They often argue because of jealousy.

explain: '강짜를 부리다'로 가장 많이 쓰고, 연인이나 부부 사이에서 상대가 다른 사람을 좋아할까 봐 샘을 내며 화를 내는 모습에 어울려요. '질투'보다 말투가 구어적이라서 조금 놀리듯이 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.example: 여자 친구가 괜히 강짜를 부려서 곤란했어요.
phrases.en: My girlfriend got jealous for no reason, and it was awkward.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질투해서 화를 내는 행동을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common expression for acting angry out of jealousy.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 강짜가 심해서 친구 만나기도 힘들어요.
phrases.en: That person is so jealous that it's hard to even meet friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질투하는 정도가 크다고 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the degree of jealousy is high.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 강짜 때문에 자주 다퉈요.
phrases.en: The two of them often argue because of jealousy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질투 때문에 싸움이 생기는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for fights that start because of jealousy.

explain_en: It is used most often as '강짜를 부리다' and fits couples or spouses who get angry out of jealousy that the partner might like someone else. It is more colloquial than '질투', so it can sound slightly teasing.

examples.en: My heart pounds loudly before a presentation.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 보자 가슴이 고동치기 시작했어요.
examples.en: As soon as I saw him, my heart started to pound.
My pounding heart gradually calmed down.
My heart pounded when I heard I had passed.

examples.ko: 너무 긴장돼서 가슴이 고동쳐서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: I was so nervous that my heart pounded and I couldn't speak.

examples.ko: 설레는 마음에 가슴이 고동치는 것 같아서 숨을 크게 쉬었어요.
examples.en: My heart seemed to pound with excitement, so I took a deep breath.

explain: 주로 '심장'이나 '가슴'이 주어로 와요. '두근거리다'가 가볍게 설레거나 긴장될 때라면 '고동치다'는 더 세고 크게 뛰는 느낌이에요. 긴장, 설렘, 감동 같은 감정을 나타내는 말로도 써요.

phrases.en: I can hear my heart pounding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 '-는'으로 바꿔 명사 '심장'을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb in the -는 form modifies the noun 심장.

phrases.en: My heart pounded hard at the news that I passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 순간의 강한 감정을 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, for a strong emotion in a moment that has passed.

phrases.en: My heart is racing as I wait for the exam results.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고동치다'보다 가볍고 일상적으로 설레거나 긴장될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter and more everyday than 고동치다, for mild excitement or nerves.

explain_en: Its subject is usually '심장' (heart) or '가슴' (chest). While '두근거리다' is for lighter excitement or nervousness, '고동치다' feels stronger, as if the heart beats big and hard. It is also used to express feelings such as tension, excitement and emotion.

t90.ax: My pounding heart gradually calmed down.

examples.ko: 이사 온 뒤로 이유 없는 공허감이 밀려와요.
examples.en: Since moving here, a feeling of emptiness washes over me for no reason.
After the big exam ended, I felt a sense of emptiness.
I felt empty in the room after my friends left.
No matter how much I eat, the emptiness doesn't get filled.
When I fall into a feeling of emptiness, I go for a walk.
Even when I threw myself into work, the emptiness didn't go away.

explain: '허전하다'는 일상에서 가볍게 쓰는 말이고, '공허감'은 마음이 텅 빈 듯한 더 깊은 느낌이라 글이나 상담에서 많이 써요. '공허감을 느끼다', '공허감이 밀려오다', '공허감을 채우다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 일이 끝나고 혼자 있을 때 공허감을 느껴요.
phrases.en: I feel emptiness when I'm alone after work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공허감'과 가장 먼저 같이 기억하면 좋은 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation to learn first with '공허감'.

phrases.example: 저는 책을 읽으면서 마음의 공허감을 채워요.
phrases.en: I fill the emptiness in my heart by reading books.
phrases.nuance_ko: 텅 빈 마음을 무언가로 달랠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when soothing an empty heart with something.

phrases.en: My friend moved away, so I feel empty inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공허감'보다 가볍고 일상적으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter, more everyday word than '공허감'.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel empty; to feel a void

explain_en: '허전하다' is a light everyday word, while '공허감' is a deeper feeling of being hollow inside and appears more in writing and counseling. It often appears in '공허감을 느끼다', '공허감이 밀려오다' and '공허감을 채우다'.

t90.ax: I felt empty in the room after my friends left.

examples.en: The sound of the wind seemed mournful all night.
The song my grandmother sings is so mournful.
The mournful sound of the flute made my heart feel heavy.

examples.ko: 구슬프도록 맑은 목소리가 오래 귓가에 남았어요.
examples.en: Her sorrowfully clear voice lingered in my ears for a long time.

examples.ko: 그 영화의 음악이 구슬퍼서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The film's music was so sorrowful that I cried.

examples.ko: 가을밤에 듣는 풀벌레 소리는 왜 이렇게 구슬플까요?
examples.en: Why do the insect sounds heard on an autumn night sound so mournful?

explain: 소리, 울음, 노래, 분위기가 슬프게 느껴질 때 주로 써요. 마음 상태 전반을 말하는 '슬프다'와 달리, 내 기분을 직접 '저는 구슬퍼요'라고 하면 어색해요. '구슬퍼요', '구슬픈'처럼 '으'가 빠지는 활용이에요.

phrases.en: A mournful cry spread through the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구슬픈'은 소리를 꾸밀 때 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 구슬픈 is most natural when describing sounds.

phrases.en: That song sounds especially sad today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 사람이 느끼는 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the mood the listener perceives.

phrases.en: This music isn't very sad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 소리나 분위기가 슬프지 않다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form: says a sound or mood is not sad.

explain_en: It is mainly used when a sound, crying, song, or atmosphere feels sad. Unlike '슬프다', which covers feelings in general, saying '저는 구슬퍼요' about your own mood sounds odd. The 'ㅡ' drops out when it is conjugated, as in '구슬퍼요' and '구슬픈'.

t90.ax: The song my grandmother sings is so mournful.

en: to promise; to set a date

examples.en: Let's part for today and look forward to next time.
We said goodbye, hoping to meet again someday.
I can't promise when I will come back.
Waiting with no end in sight is hard.
Sadly, we parted ways, promising to meet at a later time.
At graduation, my friends and I promised to meet again.

explain: '약속하다'보다 시간이 멀고 막연한 미래를 말할 때 써요. '다음을 기약하다', '훗날을 기약하다'처럼 이별이나 아쉬운 상황에서 많이 나와요. 또 '기약할 수 없다', '기약 없다'처럼 '언제 될지 모른다'는 부정형으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: With tears, we promised to meet again someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 만나자는 막연한 약속을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a vague promise to meet again.

phrases.en: He waited for news without knowing when it would come.
phrases.nuance_ko: 언제일지 모르는 채로 기다린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means waiting without knowing when it will happen.

phrases.en: I can't promise when we will meet next.
phrases.nuance_ko: 언제 될지 확신할 수 없다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form meaning you can't be sure when it will happen.

explain_en: Hopeful, vague promise about a later time, literary (재회를 기약하다) Compared with '약속하다', it is used for a distant, vague future. It often appears in parting or regretful situations, as in '다음을 기약하다' and '훗날을 기약하다'. It is also common in negative forms like '기약할 수 없다' and '기약 없다', meaning nobody knows when it will happen.

t90.ax: Waiting with no end in sight is hard.

en: to lose heart; to be dejected; to despair

examples.en: Please don't despair too much just because you failed the exam.
He was greatly disheartened when he heard the result.

examples.ko: 낙망할 때 친구의 한마디가 큰 힘이 됐어요.
examples.en: When I was in despair, a word from my friend gave me great strength.

examples.ko: 부모님이 낙망하실까 봐 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't tell them because I was afraid my parents would be crushed.

examples.ko: 한 번 실패했다고 낙망해서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't lose hope just because you failed once.
He came home with a dejected face.

explain: '실망하다'보다 희망을 잃어버린 느낌이 강해요. 말할 때는 '낙담하다'나 '실망하다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '낙망하다'는 글이나 격려하는 말에서 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: My friend failed the exam and was very discouraged.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낙망하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 말할 때 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 낙망하다, but used more often in everyday speech.

phrases.en: Don't despair just because you failed once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘내라고 격려할 때 쓰는 부정 명령 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to encourage someone.

phrases.en: He came home looking despondent.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낙망하다'를 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 낙망하다, placed before a noun.

explain_en: Stronger, losing hope after bad outcome — literary, written. It feels stronger than '실망하다' because it suggests losing hope. In speech people use '낙담하다' or '실망하다' more, while '낙망하다' shows up in writing and words of encouragement.

t90.ax: He came home with a dejected face.
